name: meeting-memory
description: Record a meeting from your browser microphone, transcribe it with Amazon Bedrock in your own AWS account, and keep searchable summaries, decisions and action items on your machine.
author: monidipa
highlights: Start, pause and stop from the app page: the browser records your mic, and optionally a shared tab's audio for remote voices
Live transcript through Bedrock speech-to-text (Mistral Voxtral by default), chunked with overlap so no word is cut
A vocabulary list steers the spelling of names, acronyms and product terms
On stop, a Bedrock LLM writes the summary, decisions, action items with owners, and open questions
Search and ask across every meeting (keyword plus Bedrock embeddings), with citations to the meeting and timestamp
MCP tools so your agent can search and read your meetings from chat
Everything is stored locally; the AWS profile is a setting, never hardcoded
useCases: Keep a searchable record of standups, design reviews and 1:1s
Ask what was decided about a topic across last month's meetings
configuration: Choose the AWS profile and region that have Bedrock access: on the app page's first screen, or run python3 scripts/configure.py --aws-profile <name> from the installed app directory. Change it later in the app's Settings.
The profile must work for the Kiro Crew gateway process (for example `aws sts get-caller-identity --profile <name>` succeeds in the shell that started the gateway).
Open the dashboard over https or http://localhost (an SSH port-forward for a remote host) so the browser allows microphone access.
